item: The task manager's History tab shows how far an errored collect run got, with the basis word on the row itself; counts the record does not carry read 'not reported', never 0
summary: Errored rows in the History tab (renderHistory, /tasks) gain one line under the error class: 'Sources processed: 17 of 20 · Articles stored: 34 · The pass stopped part-way', read from the pass_counts the run record now carries. The basis word (pass_returned, pass_raised, not_reported) is spelled out ON the row as a short phrase (the pass finished, a later step failed / the pass stopped part-way / the failure came before anything was counted), with the method and caveat in a translated hover (#oo-tip), so the reading the figures rest on is never behind the hover alone. A count the record holds as null, or a record with no pass_counts at all, reads 'not reported' and its hover says the figures are unknown and not zero; a real 0 reads 0, so the two never share a glyph; a total that is unknown is not invented (sources processed shows alone). The basis vocabulary is closed: any other word reads as not reported. Ok rows draw no line (their figures are in the result). All text is escaped, thousands go through the shared formatter (fmtNum), 10 new strings in 12 locales (canonical sorted, i18n --min 100 at 7072/7072). Enforced by tests/history_pass_counts_node_test.js (11 cases, 13 of 13 mutants killed) and tests/test_history_pass_counts.py (locales, hover, CSS, wiring). Looked at in Chromium in en, de, ar (RTL), ja and a 390 px phone; screenshots kept in the keyword-export folder. Reads only what /api/jobs/history already passes verbatim; no new endpoint and no new network.
